results.evidence: The first-ascensionist's 2015 entry lists the route as Sport with protection 'bolts', P2 then unfreed. A different climber's July 2026 comment on the route says P2 (a thin slab) was freed in 2026 and is bolted, with a piton after the crux that pulled out by hand and was not replaced, leaving extra space between bolts. Two parties agree P2 is bolted, so pro_needs, detailed_rack and the hazard line are updated; the grade stays unconfirmed (neither gives one).

results.evidence: The route's only description (Trad, 5 pitches, 400 ft, Grade II) lists the chained anchors passed (tops of Caravan and Django, the crux-pitch anchor) but says nothing about getting off the clifftop; the crag page and route comments add no descent. Whether parties rappel the route or walk off cannot be confirmed. A report of an actual descent from the top would settle it.

Alice starts from the top of Summertime P1 (itself described as passing the Caravan and Django chains) and is 40 ft, so its anchor is likely beyond a single-rope lower; but no source states the anchor height or how parties descend from it, and there are no comments. A report of the descent from the Alice anchor would settle it.

results.fact: Cairned crack passage (possibly another peak's feature)
results.evidence: A first-hand Sundial ascent describes a couloir on the right of the Needles that doglegs left to the ridge, then a short class 3 scramble south - no cliff-out or cairned crack. The Olympic climbing guide's Sundial page lists only route names (Class 3 East Face, Belvedere Basin, Surprise Basin; 5.0 South Side Face) with no detail. A Mount Clark corkscrew trip report describes ledges, a notch and an exposed diagonal crack down to an east ledge - the likely origin of the sentence - but no source states Sundial lacks such a spot. A detailed Sundial East Face description would settle it.
